content.snl: thm-hyp(list-partial(Type.judge(@F, Analysis.PFun), Type.judge(list-partial(@a, @b), Real), $#0 < #1$(a, b), Analysis.contOnIcc(F, a, b)), Logic.exists-typed(@c, Real, Logic.and(Set.mem(c, Ioo(a, b)), Analysis.deriv(F, c, Div.div(Sub.sub(Type.apply(Analysis.map(F), b), Type.apply(Analysis.map(F), a)), Sub.sub(b, a))))))
content.markdown:
Some interior point has derivative equal to the average rate of change `(F b − F a)/(b − a)`. It follows from Rolle applied to `F` minus the secant line.

This is the bridge from local to global information and the engine behind most of one-variable calculus: vanishing derivative on an interval forces constancy, a sign condition on the derivative forces monotonicity, and a bound on the derivative gives a Lipschitz estimate. Each of these is false without connectedness of the interval.
